intro: Medical transcriptionists know medical terms, type fast and catch errors, skills used across health records and office work. The closest of the 25 careers below is Medical Records Specialists, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $51,140, which is 27% more than the $40,410 transcriptionists earn.
why_it_works: Transcribing means listening carefully, applying medical vocabulary and producing accurate records on a deadline. O*NET rates judgment and time management at 3 out of 5 for this job. Records, medical office, pharmacy and court reporting jobs use the same accuracy. 24 of the 25 matches pay more, and none needs extra education. The skills to build are service orientation and persuasion.
tips: Medical records work is the closest move and uses your knowledge of medical terms and coding.
Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners earn $72,420, which is 79% more, and value fast, accurate typing.
Pharmacy Technicians earn $45,750, or 13% more, after short training.

faq.q: What jobs can former medical transcriptionists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Medical Records Specialists (88%), medical secretaries and administrative assistants (84%) and Word Processors and Typists (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Pharmacy Technicians are 81% matched and earn $45,750, which is 13% more than the $40,410 transcriptionist median.

faq.q: Which careers for medical transcriptionists pay more?
faq.a: 24 of the 25 matches pay more. Executive assistants earn $76,590 (90% more), court reporters and captioners $72,420 (79% more) and licensed practical nurses $64,400 (59% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nursing requires a program and license first.

faq.q: Do medical transcriptionists need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than medical transcriptionists already have, including all of the top 10. In a close match, 48% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and training often takes a month or less.

faq.q: What skills should medical transcriptionists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are service orientation, managing materials, persuasion and managing financial resources. Social perceptiveness already rates 2.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so patient-facing and office skills are the main steps up.
